how_rho_was_obtained.rank_T_equals_rank_V_because: T tensor Q is irreducible (step 4) and V is a nonzero sub-Hodge-structure of it (step 5)
how_rho_was_obtained.b2_source: Zarhin p.200 gives dim V(Y) = b_2(Y) - rho(Y); b_2 = 22 for a K3

tier_reason: steps 1-3 computed or directly cited; steps 5-7 formal; step 4 is a citation to two independent published sources, not re-derived here

how.source: Almkvist & van Straten, arXiv:2103.08651, 'the three sporadic third order operators'
how.s7: K3 = intersection of six hyperplane sections of G(2,6) in its Plucker embedding
how.s10: K3 = intersection of four (1,1)-type hyperplane sections in P^3 x P^3 (Segre)
how.why_it_discharges: a closed subvariety of projective space is projective

very_general_member.note: rho = 19 is the generic value; it jumps to 20 on a countable dense subset (Noether-Lefschetz locus). NOT a statement about every fibre.

irreducibility_of_T.source: Zarhin, 'Hodge groups of K3 surfaces', J. reine angew. Math. 341 (1983) 193-220
irreducibility_of_T.statement: Theorem 1.6(a), p.207: the Hdg-module V(Y) is simple
irreducibility_of_T.V_is_T: p.200: V(Y) := orthogonal complement of the algebraic-cycle lattice A(Y) in H^2(Y,Q); dim_Q V(Y) = b_2(Y) - rho(Y)
irreducibility_of_T.hypotheses: Y a smooth irreducible projective surface over C with p_g = 1; no genericity hypothesis
irreducibility_of_T.read_how: scan with no text layer; read as rendered page images (pp. 193, 200, 207)

irreducibility_of_T.statement: Lemma 3.2.7 (draft 2.7): the transcendental lattice of a polarizable Hodge structure of K3 type is a polarizable irreducible Hodge structure; Lemma 3.3.1 (draft 3.1): T(X) = NS(X)^perp, and if X is projective then T(X) is polarizable irreducible
irreducibility_of_T.minimality: Definition 3.2.5 (draft 2.5): T is the minimal primitive sub-Hodge structure with V^{2,0} = T^{2,0}
irreducibility_of_T.counterexample_without_projectivity: Example 3.3.2 (draft 3.2): for a non-projective K3, NS(X)^perp need not be irreducible
